You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: c027's cap of 31.36 is the strongest robust parent; a modest x0.5 tightening to 15.68 (the c025 value) combined with keeping the decay<=0.5 and halved ignore-degree base reduces over-weighting of the few worst nets, spreading timing weight to more moderate nets and improving TNS robustness across all circuits.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1001:HBT min-spacing violation; bp_fe-ng45/1002:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1003:legalization overlap; bp-ng45/1001:KeyError in partition; bp-ng45/1002:KeyError in partition; bp-ng45/1003:HBT min-spacing violation
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Invalid: legality (HBT min-spacing, legalization overlap), crash (KeyError in partition), and timeout failures. Systematic across all seeds of bp_fe-ng45 and bp-ng45, so this candidate says nothing about the hypothesis. To make the idea legal: keep the x0.5 cap tightening but revert the halved ignore-degree base (likely driving the partition KeyError and spacing/overlap), then re-run; if failures persist, isolate cap change alone before combining with decay/ignore-degree edits.
